correctness.rationale: The check uses the positive-frequency phase speed with finite positive depths, strictly stable density ordering, quiescent layers, rigid lids and positive tension. In y=k² the denominator D has a constant term D0=Σρ_j/h_j plus positive multiples of y/(h_j² y+π²n²), by logarithmic differentiation of the sinh product. The differentiated series are uniformly dominated by summable n^-2 and n^-4 bounds, so D'>0, D''<0 and D'(0)=Σρ_j h_j/3. Dominated convergence gives D'(∞)=0. The quantity H=D-yD' starts positive at D0 and increases, hence R=A D'/H strictly decreases from Tc to zero. The exact derivative F'=H(T−R)/D² fixes the sign on the entire positive axis, including the critical case, and gives one strict minimum below threshold. Taking the positive square root preserves the classification. At k=0 the extension has zero first derivative for every T, not just Tc; the critical case is distinguished by vanishing quadratic coefficient in k, and has no positive-wavenumber stationary point. This clarifies the endpoint wording. The frozen supporting verification is analytic; no scan, nonlinear-wave result, or bounded-range surrogate is used.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the global exclusion of extra stationary points in the subcritical regime for general unequal finite depths. The same dispersion, exact threshold, existence of the positive minimum below threshold, and an equivalent stationarity equation are all in Kadari et al. Appendix A also states that the stationary factor can vanish at positive wavenumber only below threshold; combined with its positive prefactor and the positive large-k derivative this already implies strict increase in the complementary regime. The added theorem is the analytic one-crossing proof across all positive wavenumbers below threshold, not a new threshold or a new derivative factorization. The closest inspected indexed theorem is for a different, single-layer shear model.

value.rationale: A local change in curvature does not settle which wavenumber realizes a minimal interfacial propagation speed. The result rules out additional stationary candidates at arbitrary finite depth ratios and selects one branch by a strictly monotone scalar equation. That is a natural and useful global classification of the linear dispersion, with no claim about existence or stability of nonlinear waves.
